description_en:
Akal Takht Sahib, meaning the Throne of the Timeless One, is the supreme temporal seat of Sikh authority. It was established in 1606 by Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji, the sixth Guru of the Sikhs, directly opposite Sri Harmandir Sahib in Amritsar. The creation of Akal Takht marked a defining moment in Sikh history, symbolizing the doctrine of Miri-Piri — the unity of spiritual and temporal authority. Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji constructed the Takht as a platform of justice and sovereignty, where matters of the Sikh community could be addressed and decisions taken in defense of righteousness.

Historically, Akal Takht has been the center of Sikh political and religious decision-making. It has witnessed major historical events, including the conferring of Guruship, Sarbat Khalsa gatherings, and proclamations of Hukamnamas. The Takht stands as a symbol of Sikh resistance against oppression and tyranny. During the 18th century, it became a rallying point for Sikh misls fighting Mughal persecution.

Architecturally, Akal Takht complements the spiritual serenity of Harmandir Sahib with its majestic and commanding presence. Over time, it has undergone reconstruction due to historical conflicts, yet its spiritual significance remains unchanged. Today, Akal Takht Sahib continues to guide the global Sikh community, issuing edicts and maintaining the highest seat of authority in Sikhism. Its historical, spiritual, and cultural influence permeates Sikh life, continuing to inspire devotion, moral courage, and the pursuit of justice across generations. The Takht symbolizes not only the unity of faith and governance but also the resilience and valor of the Sikh community, reminding all of the importance of courage, ethics, and adherence to righteousness.
description_pa:
ਅਕਾਲ ਤਖ਼ਤ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਦਾ ਅਰਥ ਹੈ ‘ਅਕਾਲ ਪੁਰਖ ਦਾ ਤਖ਼ਤ’। ਇਹ ਸਿੱਖ ਪੰਥ ਦਾ ਸਭ ਤੋਂ ਉੱਚਾ ਧਾਰਮਿਕ ਅਤੇ ਰਾਜਸੀ ਕੇਂਦਰ ਹੈ। ਇਸ ਦੀ ਸਥਾਪਨਾ 1606 ਵਿੱਚ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਗੁਰੂ ਹਰਿਗੋਬਿੰਦ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਜੀ ਨੇ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਹਰਿਮੰਦਰ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਦੇ ਸਾਹਮਣੇ ਕੀਤੀ। ਅਕਾਲ ਤਖ਼ਤ ਦੀ ਸਥਾਪਨਾ ਸਿੱਖ ਇਤਿਹਾਸ ਵਿੱਚ ਮੀਰੀ-ਪੀਰੀ ਦੇ ਸਿਧਾਂਤ ਦਾ ਪ੍ਰਤੀਕ ਹੈ, ਜਿਸ ਅਨੁਸਾਰ ਧਾਰਮਿਕ ਅਤੇ ਰਾਜਸੀ ਅਧਿਕਾਰ ਇਕਠੇ ਚਲਦੇ ਹਨ।

ਇਤਿਹਾਸਕ ਤੌਰ 'ਤੇ ਅਕਾਲ ਤਖ਼ਤ ਸਿੱਖ ਕੌਮ ਦੇ ਮਹੱਤਵਪੂਰਨ ਫੈਸਲਿਆਂ ਦਾ ਕੇਂਦਰ ਰਿਹਾ ਹੈ। ਇੱਥੇ ਸਰਬੱਤ ਖ਼ਾਲਸਾ ਦੇ ਇਕੱਠ ਹੋਏ, ਹੁਕਮਨਾਮੇ ਜਾਰੀ ਕੀਤੇ ਗਏ ਅਤੇ ਪੰਥਕ ਮਾਮਲਿਆਂ 'ਤੇ ਵਿਚਾਰ ਕੀਤਾ ਗਿਆ। 18ਵੀਂ ਸਦੀ ਵਿੱਚ ਮੁਗਲ ਜ਼ੁਲਮ ਦੇ ਖ਼ਿਲਾਫ਼ ਲੜਾਈ ਦੌਰਾਨ ਇਹ ਸਿੱਖ ਮਿਸਲਾਂ ਦਾ ਕੇਂਦਰ ਬਣਿਆ।

ਅਕਾਲ ਤਖ਼ਤ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਦੀ ਇਮਾਰਤ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਹਰਿਮੰਦਰ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਦੀ ਆਤਮਿਕ ਸ਼ਾਂਤੀ ਦੇ ਨਾਲ ਰਾਜਸੀ ਸ਼ਾਨ ਦਾ ਪ੍ਰਤੀਕ ਹੈ। ਸਮੇਂ-ਸਮੇਂ 'ਤੇ ਇਸ ਦੀ ਮੁੜ ਨਿਰਮਾਣ ਹੋਇਆ, ਪਰ ਇਸ ਦੀ ਮਹੱਤਤਾ ਕਦੇ ਘੱਟ ਨਹੀਂ ਹੋਈ। ਅੱਜ ਵੀ ਇਹ ਸੰਸਾਰ ਭਰ ਦੇ ਸਿੱਖਾਂ ਲਈ ਸਭ ਤੋਂ ਉੱਚਾ ਅਧਿਕਾਰਿਕ ਕੇਂਦਰ ਹੈ। ਇਹ ਤਖ਼ਤ ਸਿੱਖ ਜੀਵਨ ਵਿੱਚ ਅਧਿਆਤਮਿਕ, ਸੱਭਿਆਚਾਰਕ ਅਤੇ ਇਤਿਹਾਸਕ ਪ੍ਰਭਾਵ ਪੈਦਾ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ, ਭਗਤੀ, ਸਹਿਮਤੀ, ਅਤੇ ਨਿਆਂ ਲਈ ਪ੍ਰੇਰਣਾ ਦਿੰਦਾ ਹੈ।
description_hi:
अकाल तख़्त साहिब, जिसका अर्थ है ‘कालातीत सत्ता का सिंहासन’, सिख धर्म का सर्वोच्च सांसारिक और धार्मिक अधिकार केंद्र है। इसकी स्थापना 1606 में छठे गुरु, गुरु हरगोबिंद साहिब जी द्वारा श्री हरमंदिर साहिब के सामने अमृतसर में की गई थी। अकाल तख़्त का निर्माण सिख इतिहास में एक निर्णायक क्षण था, जो मिरी-पीरी के सिद्धांत का प्रतीक है — आध्यात्मिक और सांसारिक सत्ता का संयोजन। गुरु हरगोबिंद साहिब जी ने इसे न्याय और सत्ता के मंच के रूप में बनाया, जहाँ सिख समुदाय के महत्वपूर्ण निर्णय लिए जाते थे और धर्म और न्याय की रक्षा की जाती थी।

इतिहास में अकाल तख़्त सिख राजनीतिक और धार्मिक निर्णय लेने का केंद्र रहा है। यहाँ गुरुत्व के समर्पण, सरबत खालसा की बैठकें और हुकमनामों की घोषणाएँ हुई हैं। यह तख़्त सिख समुदाय के अत्याचार और दमन के खिलाफ प्रतिरोध का प्रतीक है। 18वीं सदी में यह मुग़ल अत्याचार के खिलाफ लड़ रहे सिख मिसलों का संगठक केंद्र बन गया।

सौंदर्य और वास्तुकला में अकाल तख़्त, हरमंदिर साहिब की आध्यात्मिक शांति के साथ मेल खाता है। समय के साथ, ऐतिहासिक संघर्षों के कारण इसे पुनर्निर्मित किया गया, पर इसकी आध्यात्मिक महत्ता अपरिवर्तित है। आज भी अकाल तख़्त साहिब दुनिया भर के सिख समुदाय का मार्गदर्शन करता है, आदेश जारी करता है और सिख धर्म में सर्वोच्च सत्ता बनाए रखता है। यह न केवल विश्वास और शासन की एकता का प्रतीक है बल्कि सिख समुदाय की धैर्य, साहस और न्यायप्रियता की याद भी दिलाता है।

description_en:
Takht Sri Kesgarh Sahib is located in Anandpur Sahib and holds immense historical significance in Sikh history. It is the birthplace of the Khalsa, established by Guru Gobind Singh Ji on the historic day of Vaisakhi in 1699. On this sacred occasion, Guru Gobind Singh Ji initiated the Panj Pyare and founded the Khalsa Panth, marking a revolutionary transformation in Sikh identity.

Kesgarh Sahib stands on a hill overlooking Anandpur Sahib, symbolizing strength and resilience. The ceremony of Amrit Sanchar first took place here, establishing the five Ks as the distinct identity of the Khalsa. This Takht represents courage, equality, and commitment to justice.

Throughout history, Anandpur Sahib witnessed numerous battles fought by Guru Gobind Singh Ji against oppressive forces. Kesgarh Sahib remains a powerful reminder of sacrifice, unity, and spiritual sovereignty. It continues to inspire Sikhs worldwide to uphold the principles of the Khalsa. The legacy of this Takht is preserved through ongoing educational, religious, and cultural activities, ensuring that the principles of bravery, equality, and devotion remain central to Sikh life. Its teachings extend beyond ritual to embody a way of life centered on service, courage, and devotion.
description_pa:
ਤਖ਼ਤ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਕੇਸਗੜ੍ਹ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਅਨੰਦਪੁਰ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਵਿੱਚ ਸਥਿਤ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਸਿੱਖ ਇਤਿਹਾਸ ਵਿੱਚ ਬਹੁਤ ਮਹੱਤਵਪੂਰਨ ਹੈ। ਇੱਥੇ 1699 ਦੀ ਵਿਸਾਖੀ ਨੂੰ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਗੁਰੂ ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ਸਿੰਘ ਜੀ ਨੇ ਖ਼ਾਲਸਾ ਪੰਥ ਦੀ ਸਥਾਪਨਾ ਕੀਤੀ ਅਤੇ ਪੰਜ ਪਿਆਰੇ ਸਾਜੇ।

ਕੇਸਗੜ੍ਹ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਅਨੰਦਪੁਰ ਦੇ ਟਿੱਬੇ 'ਤੇ ਸਥਿਤ ਹੈ ਜੋ ਸ਼ਕਤੀ ਅਤੇ ਹਿੰਮਤ ਦਾ ਪ੍ਰਤੀਕ ਹੈ। ਇੱਥੇ ਸਭ ਤੋਂ ਪਹਿਲਾਂ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤ ਸੰਚਾਰ ਹੋਇਆ ਅਤੇ ਪੰਜ ਕਕਾਰਾਂ ਦੀ ਪਰੰਪਰਾ ਸ਼ੁਰੂ ਹੋਈ। ਇਹ ਤਖ਼ਤ ਹਿੰਮਤ, ਬਰਾਬਰੀ ਅਤੇ ਨਿਆਂ ਦਾ ਪ੍ਰਤੀਕ ਹੈ।

ਅਨੰਦਪੁਰ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਨੇ ਕਈ ਇਤਿਹਾਸਕ ਯੁੱਧ ਵੇਖੇ ਜੋ ਗੁਰੂ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਨੇ ਜ਼ੁਲਮ ਦੇ ਖ਼ਿਲਾਫ਼ ਲੜੇ। ਅੱਜ ਵੀ ਇਹ ਸਿੱਖਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਖ਼ਾਲਸਾਈ ਜੀਵਨ ਦੀ ਪ੍ਰੇਰਣਾ ਦਿੰਦਾ ਹੈ।
description_hi:
तख़्त श्री केसगढ़ साहिब, अनंदपुर साहिब में स्थित है और सिख इतिहास में अत्यंत महत्वपूर्ण स्थान रखता है। यह खालसा पंथ की जन्मस्थली है, जिसकी स्थापना 1699 में गुरु गोबिंद सिंह जी ने बैसाखी के पावन दिन की। इस अवसर पर गुरु जी ने पांच प्यारे को अमृत दी और खालसा पंथ की नींव रखी, जो सिख पहचान में एक क्रांतिकारी परिवर्तन था।

केसगढ़ साहिब एक पहाड़ी पर स्थित है, जो शक्ति और साहस का प्रतीक है। यहां अमृत संचार समारोह पहली बार आयोजित हुआ और खालसा की पांच ककार परंपरा स्थापित की गई। यह तख़्त साहस, समानता और न्याय के प्रति प्रतिबद्धता का प्रतिनिधित्व करता है।

इतिहास में अनंदपुर साहिब में गुरु गोबिंद सिंह जी ने अत्याचारी शक्तियों के खिलाफ कई युद्ध लड़े। केसगढ़ साहिब बलिदान, एकता और आध्यात्मिक प्रभुत्व की याद दिलाता है। आज भी यह सिखों को खालसा के सिद्धांतों को बनाए रखने और अपने जीवन में साहस, सेवा और भक्ति के मूल्यों को अपनाने के लिए प्रेरित करता है।

description_en:
Takht Sri Damdama Sahib, located in Talwandi Sabo, is known as the Guru Ki Kashi. It is the place where Guru Gobind Singh Ji prepared the final recension of the Guru Granth Sahib in 1705. Here, Guru Sahib stayed for nearly a year and completed the compilation of the Sikh scripture by including the hymns of Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji.

Damdama Sahib became a center of learning and spiritual education. Many Sikhs gathered here to study Gurbani and Sikh philosophy. It holds immense importance as the seat of scriptural authority.

Today, Takht Sri Damdama Sahib stands as a symbol of knowledge, devotion, and literary excellence within Sikh tradition. It represents the enduring commitment of the Sikh community to preserve the Guru’s teachings accurately and pass them on to future generations. The activities at Damdama Sahib continue to inspire learning, meditation, and service to the community, fostering a culture of scholarship and piety among Sikhs worldwide.
description_pa:
ਤਖ਼ਤ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਦਮਦਮਾ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਤਲਵੰਡੀ ਸਾਬੋ ਵਿੱਚ ਸਥਿਤ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਇਸ ਨੂੰ ‘ਗੁਰੂ ਕੀ ਕਾਸ਼ੀ’ ਕਿਹਾ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ। ਇੱਥੇ 1705 ਵਿੱਚ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਗੁਰੂ ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ਸਿੰਘ ਜੀ ਨੇ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਗੁਰੂ ਗ੍ਰੰਥ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਦੀ ਅੰਤਿਮ ਸੰਪਾਦਨਾ ਕੀਤੀ ਅਤੇ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਗੁਰੂ ਤੇਗ ਬਹਾਦਰ ਜੀ ਦੀ ਬਾਣੀ ਸ਼ਾਮਲ ਕੀਤੀ।

ਇਹ ਸਥਾਨ ਸਿੱਖ ਵਿਦਿਆ ਅਤੇ ਆਤਮਿਕ ਸਿੱਖਿਆ ਦਾ ਕੇਂਦਰ ਬਣਿਆ। ਇੱਥੇ ਬਹੁਤ ਸਾਰੇ ਸਿੱਖ ਗੁਰਬਾਣੀ ਅਤੇ ਫ਼ਲਸਫ਼ਾ ਪੜ੍ਹਨ ਆਏ।

ਦਮਦਮਾ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਗਿਆਨ ਅਤੇ ਭਗਤੀ ਦਾ ਪ੍ਰਤੀਕ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਸਿੱਖ ਸਮੁਦਾਇ ਦੀ ਪ੍ਰਤੀਬੱਧਤਾ ਨੂੰ ਦਰਸਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ ਕਿ ਗੁਰੂ ਦੀ ਬਾਣੀ ਨੂੰ ਸਹੀ ਤਰੀਕੇ ਨਾਲ ਸੰਭਾਲ ਕੇ ਅਗਲੀ ਪੀੜ੍ਹੀਆਂ ਤੱਕ ਪਹੁੰਚਾਇਆ ਜਾਵੇ।
description_hi:
तख़्त श्री दमदमा साहिब, तलवंडी साबो में स्थित, गुरु की काशी के नाम से जाना जाता है। यह वही स्थान है जहाँ गुरु गोबिंद सिंह जी ने 1705 में गुरु ग्रंथ साहिब का अंतिम संस्करण तैयार किया। यहाँ गुरु साहिब लगभग एक वर्ष तक रुके और गुरु तेग बहादुर जी की बाणी को शामिल करके सिख धर्मग्रंथ की संपूर्ण तैयारी पूरी की।

दमदमा साहिब शिक्षा और आध्यात्मिक अध्ययन का केंद्र बन गया। यहाँ कई सिख गुरबाणी और सिख दर्शन का अध्ययन करने के लिए इकट्ठा हुए। यह तख़्त शास्त्रीय अधिकार और आध्यात्मिक शिक्षा का प्रतीक है। आज भी दमदमा साहिब ज्ञान, भक्ति और साहित्यिक उत्कृष्टता का प्रतीक है, और सिख समुदाय की गहरी प्रतिबद्धता को दर्शाता है कि गुरु की शिक्षाओं को सही रूप में संरक्षित किया जाए और आने वाली पीढ़ियों तक पहुँचाया जाए।

description_en:
Takht Sri Patna Sahib marks the birthplace of Guru Gobind Singh Ji in 1666. Located in Patna, Bihar, it holds immense emotional and spiritual significance for Sikhs worldwide. The early childhood of Guru Gobind Singh Ji was spent here before moving to Punjab.

The shrine preserves relics associated with Guru Sahib, including weapons and sacred items. It stands as a symbol of divine destiny and spiritual brilliance.

Patna Sahib continues to attract thousands of pilgrims annually, celebrating the birth anniversary of Guru Gobind Singh Ji with great devotion. Its legacy is a continuous source of inspiration, emphasizing humility, learning, and devotion as core aspects of Sikh life. The preservation of sacred relics and the historical narratives associated with the Guru serve as educational and spiritual guidance for generations of devotees.
description_pa:
ਤਖ਼ਤ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਪਟਨਾ ਸਾਹਿਬ 1666 ਵਿੱਚ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਗੁਰੂ ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ਸਿੰਘ ਜੀ ਦਾ ਜਨਮ ਸਥਾਨ ਹੈ। ਇਹ ਬਿਹਾਰ ਦੇ ਪਟਨਾ ਸ਼ਹਿਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਸਥਿਤ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਸਿੱਖਾਂ ਲਈ ਬਹੁਤ ਪਵਿੱਤਰ ਹੈ।

ਇੱਥੇ ਗੁਰੂ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਨਾਲ ਸੰਬੰਧਿਤ ਅਨੇਕ ਪਵਿੱਤਰ ਨਿਸ਼ਾਨੀਆਂ ਸੰਭਾਲ ਕੇ ਰੱਖੀਆਂ ਗਈਆਂ ਹਨ।

ਹਰ ਸਾਲ ਇੱਥੇ ਗੁਰੂ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਦੇ ਪ੍ਰਕਾਸ਼ ਪੁਰਬ 'ਤੇ ਵੱਡੀ ਗਿਣਤੀ ਵਿੱਚ ਸੰਗਤ ਇਕੱਠੀ ਹੁੰਦੀ ਹੈ।
description_hi:
तख़्त श्री पटना साहिब, 1666 में गुरु गोबिंद सिंह जी का जन्मस्थान है। यह बिहार के पटना शहर में स्थित है और सिखों के लिए अत्यंत पवित्र और भावनात्मक रूप से महत्वपूर्ण है। गुरु गोबिंद सिंह जी का प्रारंभिक बचपन यहीं बीता, इसके बाद वे पंजाब गए।

इस स्थान पर गुरु साहिब से संबंधित कई पवित्र अवशेष, जैसे अस्त्र-शस्त्र और धार्मिक वस्तुएँ सुरक्षित रखी गई हैं। यह तख़्त दिव्य नियति और आध्यात्मिक प्रतिभा का प्रतीक है। हर साल हजारों श्रद्धालु यहाँ आते हैं और गुरु गोबिंद सिंह जी के जन्मदिवस को बड़े श्रद्धा भाव से मनाते हैं। यह स्थल सिख जीवन के कोर मूल्यों — विनम्रता, शिक्षा और भक्ति — का प्रेरक स्रोत है।

description_en:
Takht Sri Hazur Sahib, located in Nanded, Maharashtra, marks the place where Guru Gobind Singh Ji left his physical form in 1708. Before his departure, Guru Sahib declared Guru Granth Sahib as the eternal Guru of the Sikhs. This moment defined the future of Sikh spiritual authority.

Hazur Sahib preserves many sacred weapons and historical relics of Guru Gobind Singh Ji. The Takht reflects the warrior spirit and spiritual authority of the Guru.

Today, it stands as a sacred pilgrimage site representing devotion, sacrifice, and eternal Guruship of Guru Granth Sahib. The site continues to educate devotees about the historical, spiritual, and ethical values exemplified by Guru Gobind Singh Ji. Pilgrims are inspired to follow a life of courage, service, and adherence to Sikh principles.
description_pa:
ਤਖ਼ਤ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਹਜ਼ੂਰ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਨੰਦੇੜ ਵਿੱਚ ਸਥਿਤ ਹੈ ਜਿੱਥੇ 1708 ਵਿੱਚ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਗੁਰੂ ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ਸਿੰਘ ਜੀ ਜੋਤਿ ਜੋਤ ਸਮਾਏ। ਇੱਥੇ ਗੁਰੂ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਨੇ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਗੁਰੂ ਗ੍ਰੰਥ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਨੂੰ ਸਦੀਵੀ ਗੁਰੂ ਘੋਸ਼ਿਤ ਕੀਤਾ।

ਇਸ ਤਖ਼ਤ 'ਤੇ ਗੁਰੂ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਦੀਆਂ ਅਸਲ ਸ਼ਸਤਰਾਂ ਅਤੇ ਨਿਸ਼ਾਨੀਆਂ ਸੰਭਾਲੀਆਂ ਗਈਆਂ ਹਨ।

ਇਹ ਸਥਾਨ ਸਿੱਖਾਂ ਲਈ ਭਗਤੀ ਅਤੇ ਬਲਿਦਾਨ ਦਾ ਪ੍ਰਤੀਕ ਹੈ।
description_hi:
तख़्त श्री हज़ूर साहिब, नांदेड़, महाराष्ट्र में स्थित है, वह स्थान जहाँ 1708 में गुरु गोबिंद सिंह जी ने अपना भौतिक शरीर त्यागा। अपने निधन से पहले, गुरु साहिब ने गुरु ग्रंथ साहिब को सिखों का शाश्वत गुरु घोषित किया। यह क्षण सिख आध्यात्मिक अधिकार की दिशा निर्धारित करता है।

हज़ूर साहिब में गुरु गोबिंद सिंह जी के कई पवित्र अस्त्र-शस्त्र और ऐतिहासिक अवशेष संरक्षित हैं। यह तख़्त गुरु की योद्धा आत्मा और आध्यात्मिक अधिकार का प्रतीक है।

आज यह एक पवित्र तीर्थ स्थल के रूप में खड़ा है, जो भक्ति, बलिदान और गुरु ग्रंथ साहिब की शाश्वत गुरुत्वता का प्रतिनिधित्व करता है। यहाँ आने वाले श्रद्धालु साहस, सेवा और सिख सिद्धांतों का पालन करने के लिए प्रेरित होते हैं।

description_en:
Gurdwara Sis Ganj Sahib, located in the historic area of Chandni Chowk in Delhi, is one of the most revered Sikh shrines in India. This sacred site marks the exact place where Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji, the ninth Sikh Guru, was martyred in 1675 by the Mughal emperor Aurangzeb for defending the religious freedom of Kashmiri Pandits and upholding the principle of universal human rights.

The martyrdom of Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji stands as a unique and unparalleled sacrifice in world history. Unlike many historical sacrifices that were made for one's own community or faith, Guru Sahib gave his life for the protection of another religion. This act demonstrated the Sikh principle of 'Sarbat da Bhala' (welfare of all) and established a powerful example of standing against injustice and tyranny.

Historically, the area where the Gurdwara now stands was a public execution ground during the Mughal period. Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji was publicly beheaded here after refusing to convert to Islam. His three devoted companions—Bhai Mati Das Ji, Bhai Sati Das Ji, and Bhai Dayala Ji—were also brutally executed in Delhi for their unwavering faith and loyalty. Their martyrdoms are remembered as acts of immense courage and devotion.

After the execution, a brave Sikh named Bhai Jaita Ji (later known as Bhai Jiwan Singh Ji) risked his life to carry the severed head (Sis) of Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji from Delhi to Anandpur Sahib. Meanwhile, another devotee, Lakhi Shah Vanjara, secretly cremated the Guru's body by setting his own house on fire to avoid Mughal interference. These acts of devotion and bravery are deeply embedded in Sikh history.

The Gurdwara Sis Ganj Sahib was later built in 1783 by Sardar Baghel Singh, a prominent Sikh general, when Sikh forces briefly took control of Delhi. He constructed several historical Gurdwaras in Delhi to commemorate important Sikh events, and Sis Ganj Sahib became one of the most significant among them.

The architecture of the Gurdwara reflects a blend of Mughal and Sikh styles, with a prominent golden dome and a serene interior that provides a spiritual atmosphere for devotees. Within the complex, certain historical elements have been preserved, including a section of the tree under which Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji was executed and a well that existed during that time. These relics serve as powerful reminders of the events that took place here.

Today, Gurdwara Sis Ganj Sahib is a major pilgrimage destination attracting thousands of devotees daily from across India and around the world. The Gurdwara offers continuous recitation of Gurbani (Akhand Path), kirtan (devotional singing), and langar (community kitchen), which serves free meals to all visitors regardless of caste, creed, or religion.

The site is not only a place of worship but also a symbol of courage, sacrifice, and religious freedom. It educates visitors about the importance of standing for truth, protecting the rights of others, and maintaining faith even in the face of extreme adversity.

Visitors often describe a deep sense of peace and spiritual connection when they enter the Gurdwara premises, despite its location in one of the busiest markets in Delhi. The contrast between the outer chaos of Chandni Chowk and the inner calm of the Gurdwara symbolizes the Sikh teaching of inner peace amidst worldly challenges.

Gurdwara Sis Ganj Sahib continues to inspire generations with the legacy of Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji, reminding humanity of the timeless values of justice, tolerance, and selfless sacrifice.
description_pa:
ਗੁਰਦੁਆਰਾ ਸੀਸ ਗੰਜ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਚਾਂਦਨੀ ਚੌਂਕ, ਦਿੱਲੀ ਵਿੱਚ ਸਥਿਤ ਸਿੱਖ ਧਰਮ ਦੇ ਸਭ ਤੋਂ ਪਵਿੱਤਰ ਸਥਾਨਾਂ ਵਿੱਚੋਂ ਇੱਕ ਹੈ। ਇਹ ਓਹੀ ਥਾਂ ਹੈ ਜਿੱਥੇ 1675 ਵਿੱਚ ਨੌਵੇਂ ਸਿੱਖ ਗੁਰੂ, ਸ੍ਰੀ ਗੁਰੂ ਤੇਗ ਬਹਾਦਰ ਜੀ ਨੂੰ ਮੁਗਲ ਬਾਦਸ਼ਾਹ ਔਰੰਗਜ਼ੇਬ ਦੇ ਹੁਕਮ 'ਤੇ ਸ਼ਹੀਦ ਕੀਤਾ ਗਿਆ ਸੀ। ਗੁਰੂ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਨੇ ਕਸ਼ਮੀਰੀ ਪੰਡਿਤਾਂ ਦੀ ਧਾਰਮਿਕ ਆਜ਼ਾਦੀ ਦੀ ਰੱਖਿਆ ਲਈ ਆਪਣੀ ਜਾਨ ਨਿਛਾਵਰ ਕੀਤੀ।

ਗੁਰੂ ਤੇਗ ਬਹਾਦਰ ਜੀ ਦੀ ਸ਼ਹਾਦਤ ਵਿਸ਼ਵ ਇਤਿਹਾਸ ਵਿੱਚ ਇਕ ਅਦੁੱਤੀ ਮਿਸਾਲ ਹੈ। ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੇ ਆਪਣੇ ਧਰਮ ਲਈ ਨਹੀਂ, ਸਗੋਂ ਹੋਰ ਧਰਮ ਦੀ ਰੱਖਿਆ ਲਈ ਕੁਰਬਾਨੀ ਦਿੱਤੀ, ਜੋ 'ਸਰਬੱਤ ਦਾ ਭਲਾ' ਦੇ ਸਿੱਧਾਂਤ ਨੂੰ ਦਰਸਾਉਂਦੀ ਹੈ।

ਮੁਗਲ ਸਮੇਂ ਦੌਰਾਨ ਇਹ ਥਾਂ ਜਨਤਕ ਫਾਂਸੀ ਦਾ ਮੈਦਾਨ ਸੀ। ਇੱਥੇ ਗੁਰੂ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਦਾ ਸੀਸ ਕੱਟਿਆ ਗਿਆ। ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦੇ ਸਾਥੀਆਂ ਭਾਈ ਮਤੀ ਦਾਸ ਜੀ, ਭਾਈ ਸਤੀ ਦਾਸ ਜੀ ਅਤੇ ਭਾਈ ਦਿਆਲਾ ਜੀ ਨੇ ਵੀ ਅਟੱਲ ਵਿਸ਼ਵਾਸ ਨਾਲ ਸ਼ਹਾਦਤ ਦਿੱਤੀ।

ਭਾਈ ਜੈਤਾ ਜੀ ਨੇ ਗੁਰੂ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਦਾ ਸੀਸ ਅਨੰਦਪੁਰ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਲੈ ਜਾ ਕੇ ਸੰਭਾਲਿਆ, ਜਦਕਿ ਲੱਖੀ ਸ਼ਾਹ ਵਣਜਾਰਾ ਨੇ ਆਪਣਾ ਘਰ ਸਾੜ ਕੇ ਗੁਰੂ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਦੇ ਧੜ ਦਾ ਸੰਸਕਾਰ ਕੀਤਾ।

1783 ਵਿੱਚ ਸਰਦਾਰ ਬਘੇਲ ਸਿੰਘ ਨੇ ਇਸ ਗੁਰਦੁਆਰੇ ਦੀ ਸਥਾਪਨਾ ਕੀਤੀ। ਅੱਜ ਇਹ ਸਥਾਨ ਭਗਤੀ, ਸ਼ਹਾਦਤ ਅਤੇ ਧਾਰਮਿਕ ਆਜ਼ਾਦੀ ਦਾ ਪ੍ਰਤੀਕ ਹੈ। ਇੱਥੇ ਰੋਜ਼ਾਨਾ ਲੰਗਰ, ਕੀਰਤਨ ਅਤੇ ਪਾਠ ਹੁੰਦਾ ਹੈ ਜੋ ਸਭ ਲਈ ਖੁੱਲਾ ਹੈ।
description_hi:
गुरुद्वारा सीस गंज साहिब, चांदनी चौक, दिल्ली में स्थित सिख धर्म के सबसे पवित्र स्थलों में से एक है। यह वही स्थान है जहाँ 1675 में नौवें सिख गुरु, गुरु तेग बहादुर जी को मुगल बादशाह औरंगज़ेब के आदेश पर शहीद किया गया था। गुरु साहिब ने कश्मीरी पंडितों की धार्मिक स्वतंत्रता की रक्षा के लिए अपना बलिदान दिया।

गुरु तेग बहादुर जी का बलिदान विश्व इतिहास में अद्वितीय है। उन्होंने अपने धर्म के लिए नहीं, बल्कि दूसरे धर्म की रक्षा के लिए प्राण न्यौछावर किए, जो 'सरबत दा भला' के सिद्धांत को दर्शाता है।

मुगल काल में यह स्थान सार्वजनिक फांसी का स्थल था। यहाँ गुरु साहिब का सिर कलम किया गया। उनके साथियों भाई मती दास जी, भाई सती दास जी और भाई दयाला जी ने भी अडिग आस्था के साथ बलिदान दिया।

भाई जैता जी गुरु साहिब का शीश आनंदपुर साहिब ले गए, जबकि लखी शाह वंजारा ने अपने घर को जलाकर गुरु साहिब के शरीर का अंतिम संस्कार किया।

1783 में सरदार बघेल सिंह ने इस गुरुद्वारे का निर्माण करवाया। आज यह स्थल भक्ति, बलिदान और धार्मिक स्वतंत्रता का प्रतीक है। यहाँ प्रतिदिन लंगर, कीर्तन और पाठ होता है जो सभी के लिए खुला है।

description_en:
Gurdwara Bangla Sahib, located near Connaught Place in the heart of New Delhi, is one of the most prominent and revered Sikh shrines in India. This sacred site is associated with Guru Har Krishan Ji, the eighth Sikh Guru, who stayed here in 1664 during his visit to Delhi. The Gurdwara stands as a symbol of compassion, humility, and selfless service, reflecting the divine spirit of the young Guru.

Originally, this site was a grand bungalow (bangla) belonging to Raja Jai Singh of Amber, a Rajput ruler and devotee of the Sikh Gurus. When Guru Har Krishan Ji arrived in Delhi, he was invited to stay at this residence. Over time, this place became sanctified due to the Guru's presence, and it later came to be known as 'Bangla Sahib.'

During Guru Har Krishan Ji’s stay in Delhi, a severe epidemic of smallpox and cholera broke out, causing immense suffering among the local population. Despite his young age, the Guru displayed extraordinary compassion and courage. He dedicated himself to serving the sick and the suffering, providing them with comfort, care, and spiritual solace.

It is believed that Guru Har Krishan Ji blessed the water of a well located within the premises of the bungalow. This water, known today as 'Amrit' from the Sarovar, was distributed among the sick and is said to have miraculous healing properties. Many people who consumed this water recovered from their illnesses, strengthening the faith of the devotees.

In serving others selflessly, Guru Har Krishan Ji himself contracted the illness. Despite his deteriorating health, he continued to guide and bless his followers. Before leaving his physical form, he uttered the words 'Baba Bakale,' indicating that the next Guru would be found in the village of Bakala. This message later led to the recognition of Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji as the ninth Sikh Guru.

The present structure of Gurdwara Bangla Sahib was built in the 18th century and later expanded and renovated over time. Maharaja Jai Singh’s bungalow was transformed into a magnificent Gurdwara, featuring a large golden dome, tall Nishan Sahib (Sikh flag), and a vast Sarovar (holy water tank) that attracts devotees from all over the world.

The Sarovar at Bangla Sahib is one of its most distinguishing features. Devotees often take a sip of the holy water or sprinkle it on themselves as a symbol of faith and spiritual cleansing. The calm and serene environment of the Sarovar offers a peaceful retreat amidst the bustling city.

The Gurdwara complex also houses a school, a hospital, a museum, and a library, all of which reflect the Sikh commitment to education, service, and community welfare. One of the most remarkable aspects of Bangla Sahib is its Langar (community kitchen), which serves free meals to thousands of people every day, regardless of religion, caste, or social status. Volunteers from all walks of life participate in preparing and serving the food, embodying the principle of 'Seva' (selfless service).

Kirtan (devotional singing of Gurbani) is performed continuously inside the main prayer hall, creating a deeply spiritual atmosphere. The soothing recitation of Gurbani provides inner peace and spiritual upliftment to visitors.

Gurdwara Bangla Sahib is not only a place of worship but also a center of humanitarian service and spiritual learning. It stands as a reminder of Guru Har Krishan Ji’s teachings of compassion, humility, and service to humanity.

Visitors often describe a profound sense of calm and divine presence upon entering the Gurdwara. The contrast between the busy streets of Delhi and the peaceful ambiance within the complex symbolizes the Sikh teaching of maintaining inner peace amidst worldly chaos.

Today, Gurdwara Bangla Sahib continues to inspire millions with its message of love, equality, and service. It remains a beacon of hope and faith, encouraging people to live a life of kindness, humility, and devotion to the welfare of all humanity.
description_pa:
ਗੁਰਦੁਆਰਾ ਬੰਗਲਾ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਨਵੀਂ ਦਿੱਲੀ ਦੇ ਕਨਾਟ ਪਲੇਸ ਨੇੜੇ ਸਥਿਤ ਸਿੱਖ ਧਰਮ ਦੇ ਸਭ ਤੋਂ ਪ੍ਰਸਿੱਧ ਤੀਰਥ ਸਥਾਨਾਂ ਵਿੱਚੋਂ ਇੱਕ ਹੈ। ਇਹ ਥਾਂ ਅੱਠਵੇਂ ਸਿੱਖ ਗੁਰੂ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਗੁਰੂ ਹਰਕ੍ਰਿਸ਼ਨ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਜੀ ਨਾਲ ਸੰਬੰਧਿਤ ਹੈ, ਜੋ 1664 ਵਿੱਚ ਇੱਥੇ ਰਹੇ ਸਨ।

ਇਹ ਸਥਾਨ ਪਹਿਲਾਂ ਰਾਜਾ ਜੈ ਸਿੰਘ ਦਾ ਬੰਗਲਾ ਸੀ, ਜਿਸ ਨੂੰ ਬਾਅਦ ਵਿੱਚ ਗੁਰਦੁਆਰੇ ਵਿੱਚ ਬਦਲ ਦਿੱਤਾ ਗਿਆ।

ਗੁਰੂ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਦੇ ਸਮੇਂ ਦੌਰਾਨ ਦਿੱਲੀ ਵਿੱਚ ਚਮੜੀ ਦੀ ਬਿਮਾਰੀ ਅਤੇ ਕਾਲਰਾ ਫੈਲਿਆ ਹੋਇਆ ਸੀ। ਗੁਰੂ ਹਰਕ੍ਰਿਸ਼ਨ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਜੀ ਨੇ ਬਿਮਾਰ ਲੋਕਾਂ ਦੀ ਸੇਵਾ ਕੀਤੀ ਅਤੇ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਆਤਮਿਕ ਸਹਾਰਾ ਦਿੱਤਾ।

ਗੁਰੂ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਨੇ ਇੱਥੇ ਦੇ ਕੁਏਂ ਦੇ ਪਾਣੀ ਨੂੰ ਅਸ਼ੀਰਵਾਦ ਦਿੱਤਾ ਜੋ ਅੱਜ ਵੀ ਸਰੋਵਰ ਦੇ ਰੂਪ ਵਿੱਚ ਮੌਜੂਦ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਲੋਕ ਇਸ ਨੂੰ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤ ਸਮਝ ਕੇ ਪ੍ਰਾਪਤ ਕਰਦੇ ਹਨ।

ਗੁਰੂ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਨੇ ਸੇਵਾ ਕਰਦਿਆਂ ਆਪ ਵੀ ਬਿਮਾਰੀ ਦਾ ਸ਼ਿਕਾਰ ਹੋ ਗਏ ਅਤੇ ਜੋਤਿ ਜੋਤ ਸਮਾ ਗਏ। ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੇ 'ਬਾਬਾ ਬਕਾਲੇ' ਦੇ ਸ਼ਬਦ ਕਹੇ, ਜਿਸ ਨਾਲ ਅਗਲੇ ਗੁਰੂ ਦੀ ਪਹਿਚਾਣ ਹੋਈ।

ਅੱਜ ਇਹ ਗੁਰਦੁਆਰਾ ਸੇਵਾ, ਭਗਤੀ ਅਤੇ ਸਮਾਨਤਾ ਦਾ ਪ੍ਰਤੀਕ ਹੈ। ਇੱਥੇ ਰੋਜ਼ਾਨਾ ਲੰਗਰ, ਕੀਰਤਨ ਅਤੇ ਸੇਵਾ ਹੁੰਦੀ ਹੈ ਜੋ ਹਰ ਕਿਸੇ ਲਈ ਖੁੱਲੀ ਹੈ।
description_hi:
गुरुद्वारा बंगला साहिब, नई दिल्ली के कनॉट प्लेस के पास स्थित सिख धर्म का एक प्रमुख तीर्थ स्थल है। यह स्थान आठवें सिख गुरु, गुरु हर कृष्ण जी से संबंधित है, जो 1664 में यहाँ ठहरे थे।

यह स्थान पहले राजा जय सिंह का बंगला था, जिसे बाद में गुरुद्वारे में परिवर्तित किया गया।

गुरु हर कृष्ण जी के समय दिल्ली में चेचक और हैजा जैसी बीमारियाँ फैली हुई थीं। गुरु जी ने बीमारों की सेवा की और उन्हें आध्यात्मिक सांत्वना दी।

गुरु जी ने यहाँ के कुएँ के जल को आशीर्वाद दिया, जो आज सरोवर के रूप में मौजूद है और श्रद्धालु इसे अमृत के रूप में ग्रहण करते हैं।

सेवा करते हुए गुरु जी स्वयं भी बीमार हो गए और उन्होंने 'बाबा बकाले' कहकर अगले गुरु का संकेत दिया।

आज यह गुरुद्वारा सेवा, भक्ति और समानता का प्रतीक है। यहाँ प्रतिदिन लंगर, कीर्तन और सेवा होती है जो सभी के लिए खुली है।

description_en:
Gurdwara Fatehgarh Sahib, located in the historic town of Sirhind in Punjab, is one of the most sacred Sikh shrines associated with the martyrdom of the younger sons of Guru Gobind Singh Ji—Sahibzada Zorawar Singh Ji and Sahibzada Fateh Singh Ji. This holy site marks the place where these innocent children were bricked alive by the Mughal authorities in 1705 under the orders of Nawab Wazir Khan of Sirhind.

The story of Fatehgarh Sahib is one of unparalleled courage, faith, and sacrifice. After the evacuation of Anandpur Sahib during difficult times, the younger Sahibzadas, along with their grandmother Mata Gujri Ji, were separated from the main group and eventually betrayed and captured by Gangu, a former servant. They were handed over to the Mughal authorities in Sirhind.

Despite their tender age—Sahibzada Zorawar Singh Ji being around nine years old and Sahibzada Fateh Singh Ji only about seven—the young princes displayed extraordinary bravery and unwavering faith. They were presented before Nawab Wazir Khan and were offered wealth, comfort, and high status if they agreed to convert to Islam. However, the Sahibzadas firmly refused, choosing instead to remain steadfast in their Sikh faith.

The Mughal authorities subjected them to immense psychological pressure and threats, but the young Sahibzadas did not waver. Their courage astonished even the courtiers present in the court. Ultimately, Wazir Khan ordered that the children be bricked alive within a wall. As the wall was being built around them, they continued to recite the name of Waheguru with calmness and courage.

When the wall collapsed, it is said that the Sahibzadas were executed. Their martyrdom is remembered as one of the most heart-wrenching and inspiring episodes in Sikh history. Their sacrifice symbolizes the ultimate commitment to faith and righteousness, even in the face of extreme cruelty.

Mata Gujri Ji, upon hearing the news of her grandsons’ martyrdom, also left her physical body in the Thanda Burj (cold tower), where she had been imprisoned. Her sacrifice is equally revered and remembered with deep respect.

Gurdwara Fatehgarh Sahib was later established at the site to commemorate this tragic yet inspiring event. The term 'Fatehgarh' translates to 'Fort of Victory,' symbolizing the spiritual victory of the Sahibzadas over oppression and injustice. Though physically defeated, their faith emerged victorious, inspiring generations to stand for truth and righteousness.

The architecture of the Gurdwara is simple yet deeply spiritual. The white marble structure, serene environment, and sacred atmosphere create a sense of reverence and reflection for visitors. The complex includes several related historical sites such as the Thanda Burj, where Mata Gujri Ji was kept, and Gurdwara Jyoti Swarup, where the final rites of the Sahibzadas were performed.

Every year in December, a grand Shaheedi Jor Mela is held at Fatehgarh Sahib to commemorate the martyrdom of the Sahibzadas and Mata Gujri Ji. Thousands of devotees from across the world gather to pay their respects, participate in kirtan, listen to katha (religious discourse), and remember the sacrifices made for the preservation of faith and justice.

The Gurdwara also continues the Sikh tradition of Langar, serving free meals to all visitors regardless of background. This practice reinforces the message of equality, unity, and selfless service.

Visiting Gurdwara Fatehgarh Sahib is a deeply emotional experience. Devotees often reflect on the immense courage shown by the young Sahibzadas and are inspired to live a life guided by faith, truth, and moral strength.

This sacred site stands as a powerful reminder that true victory lies not in worldly power but in spiritual strength and unwavering commitment to righteousness. The legacy of Sahibzada Zorawar Singh Ji and Sahibzada Fateh Singh Ji continues to inspire millions, reminding humanity of the enduring power of faith, courage, and sacrifice.
description_pa:
ਗੁਰਦੁਆਰਾ ਫਤਿਹਗੜ੍ਹ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਪੰਜਾਬ ਦੇ ਸਿਰਹਿੰਦ ਵਿੱਚ ਸਥਿਤ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਇਹ ਸਿੱਖ ਇਤਿਹਾਸ ਦਾ ਇੱਕ ਮਹੱਤਵਪੂਰਨ ਸਥਾਨ ਹੈ ਜਿੱਥੇ ਗੁਰੂ ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ਸਿੰਘ ਜੀ ਦੇ ਛੋਟੇ ਸਾਹਿਬਜ਼ਾਦੇ, ਸਾਹਿਬਜ਼ਾਦਾ ਜ਼ੋਰਾਵਰ ਸਿੰਘ ਜੀ ਅਤੇ ਸਾਹਿਬਜ਼ਾਦਾ ਫਤਿਹ ਸਿੰਘ ਜੀ ਨੂੰ 1705 ਵਿੱਚ ਸ਼ਹੀਦ ਕੀਤਾ ਗਿਆ ਸੀ।

ਨਵਾਬ ਵਜ਼ੀਰ ਖਾਨ ਨੇ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਇਸਲਾਮ ਕਬੂਲ ਕਰਨ ਲਈ ਕਿਹਾ, ਪਰ ਛੋਟੀ ਉਮਰ ਦੇ ਬਾਵਜੂਦ ਸਾਹਿਬਜ਼ਾਦਿਆਂ ਨੇ ਅਟੱਲ ਵਿਸ਼ਵਾਸ ਦਿਖਾਇਆ ਅਤੇ ਇਨਕਾਰ ਕਰ ਦਿੱਤਾ।

ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਜੀਉਂਦੇ ਹੀ ਦੀਵਾਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਚੁਣਵਾ ਦਿੱਤਾ ਗਿਆ। ਇਹ ਸ਼ਹਾਦਤ ਸਿੱਖ ਇਤਿਹਾਸ ਦੀ ਸਭ ਤੋਂ ਦੁਖਦਾਈ ਅਤੇ ਪ੍ਰੇਰਣਾਦਾਇਕ ਘਟਨਾਵਾਂ ਵਿੱਚੋਂ ਇੱਕ ਹੈ।

ਮਾਤਾ ਗੁਜਰੀ ਜੀ ਨੇ ਵੀ ਠੰਢੇ ਬੁਰਜ ਵਿੱਚ ਆਪਣੇ ਪ੍ਰਾਣ ਤਿਆਗ ਦਿੱਤੇ।

ਅੱਜ ਇਹ ਗੁਰਦੁਆਰਾ ਸ਼ਹਾਦਤ, ਵਿਸ਼ਵਾਸ ਅਤੇ ਸੱਚ ਦੀ ਜਿੱਤ ਦਾ ਪ੍ਰਤੀਕ ਹੈ। ਹਰ ਸਾਲ ਦਸੰਬਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਇੱਥੇ ਸ਼ਹੀਦੀ ਜੋੜ ਮੇਲਾ ਲੱਗਦਾ ਹੈ।
description_hi:
गुरुद्वारा फतेहगढ़ साहिब पंजाब के सिरहिंद में स्थित एक अत्यंत पवित्र सिख स्थल है, जहाँ गुरु गोबिंद सिंह जी के छोटे साहिबज़ादे—साहिबज़ादा जोरावर सिंह जी और साहिबज़ादा फतेह सिंह जी—को 1705 में शहीद किया गया था।

नवाब वज़ीर खान ने उन्हें इस्लाम स्वीकार करने के लिए कहा, लेकिन छोटी उम्र के बावजूद उन्होंने अपने धर्म को नहीं छोड़ा।

उन्हें जीवित ही दीवार में चुनवा दिया गया। यह घटना सिख इतिहास की सबसे मार्मिक और प्रेरणादायक घटनाओं में से एक है।

माता गुजरी जी ने भी ठंडे बुर्ज में अपने प्राण त्याग दिए।

आज यह गुरुद्वारा बलिदान, आस्था और सत्य की विजय का प्रतीक है। हर वर्ष दिसंबर में यहाँ शहीदी जोड़ मेला आयोजित होता है।

description_en:
Gurdwara Shaheed Ganj Sahib, located in the sacred city of Amritsar, Punjab, stands as a powerful symbol of Sikh martyrdom, resilience, and unwavering faith. This historic shrine commemorates the sacrifices of numerous Sikh martyrs who laid down their lives in the face of oppression, particularly during the turbulent 18th century when Sikhs were subjected to severe persecution under Mughal rule.

The term 'Shaheed Ganj' literally translates to 'the place of martyrs,' and the Gurdwara truly lives up to this name. It is believed to be one of the sites where the severed heads (shaheeds' remains) of Sikh warriors were brought and respectfully cremated after they were executed by the authorities. These martyrs included brave Sikhs who refused to abandon their faith despite facing brutal torture and death.

During the 18th century, the Mughal administration, along with local governors like Zakariya Khan, launched systematic campaigns to suppress the growing Sikh community. Rewards were announced for capturing or killing Sikhs, forcing many to live in jungles and remote areas while continuing their struggle for religious freedom and justice.

Captured Sikhs were often brought to places like Lahore and Amritsar, where they were publicly executed. Their bodies were sometimes desecrated, but devoted Sikhs risked their lives to recover the remains of the martyrs and perform their last rites with honor. Gurdwara Shaheed Ganj Sahib is associated with such acts of devotion and bravery.

One of the most notable figures connected to the history of Sikh martyrdom is Bhai Mani Singh Ji, a revered Sikh scholar and martyr. Although his martyrdom took place in Lahore, his legacy is closely tied to the broader narrative of Sikh sacrifices commemorated at Shaheed Ganj Sahib. Bhai Mani Singh Ji was executed for refusing to convert and for upholding Sikh traditions, becoming an enduring symbol of faith and courage.

The Gurdwara was established to honor the memory of these countless unnamed and known martyrs who sacrificed their lives to protect the Sikh faith and its principles. Over time, it became a place of reflection, remembrance, and inspiration for Sikhs and visitors from around the world.

Architecturally, Gurdwara Shaheed Ganj Sahib is characterized by its serene white marble structure and peaceful surroundings. Though not as grand as some of the larger Gurdwaras, its spiritual significance is immense. The simplicity of the structure reflects the humility and sacrifice of the martyrs it commemorates.

Inside the Gurdwara, continuous recitation of Gurbani and kirtan creates an atmosphere of deep spiritual connection. Devotees come here to pay their respects, offer prayers, and reflect on the sacrifices made by their forefathers.

The Gurdwara also upholds the Sikh tradition of Langar, providing free meals to all visitors regardless of their background. This practice reinforces the core Sikh values of equality, service, and community bonding.

Visiting Gurdwara Shaheed Ganj Sahib is a deeply emotional experience. The site serves as a reminder of a time when maintaining one's faith required immense courage and resilience. It inspires individuals to stand firm in their beliefs and to uphold truth and justice, even in the face of adversity.

The legacy of the martyrs remembered at Shaheed Ganj Sahib continues to influence Sikh identity and values. Their sacrifices are not only remembered in history but are also celebrated in daily prayers and community life.

Today, the Gurdwara stands as a beacon of remembrance and inspiration, reminding humanity of the cost of freedom and the power of unwavering faith. It encourages visitors to live with integrity, courage, and a commitment to the welfare of all, embodying the true spirit of Sikhism.
description_pa:
ਗੁਰਦੁਆਰਾ ਸ਼ਹੀਦ ਗੰਜ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤਸਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਸਥਿਤ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਇਹ ਸਿੱਖ ਸ਼ਹੀਦਾਂ ਦੀ ਯਾਦ ਵਿੱਚ ਬਣਾਇਆ ਗਿਆ ਪਵਿੱਤਰ ਸਥਾਨ ਹੈ। 'ਸ਼ਹੀਦ ਗੰਜ' ਦਾ ਅਰਥ ਹੈ ਸ਼ਹੀਦਾਂ ਦਾ ਸਥਾਨ।

18ਵੀਂ ਸਦੀ ਦੌਰਾਨ ਮੁਗਲ ਹਕੂਮਤ ਵੱਲੋਂ ਸਿੱਖਾਂ 'ਤੇ ਕਾਫੀ ਜ਼ੁਲਮ ਕੀਤੇ ਗਏ। ਬਹੁਤ ਸਾਰੇ ਸਿੱਖਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਕੈਦ ਕਰਕੇ ਮਾਰਿਆ ਗਿਆ, ਪਰ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੇ ਆਪਣੇ ਧਰਮ ਤੋਂ ਮੂੰਹ ਨਹੀਂ ਮੋੜਿਆ।

ਸ਼ਹੀਦਾਂ ਦੇ ਸਿਰ ਅਤੇ ਸਰੀਰਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਸਿੱਖ ਭਗਤਾਂ ਵੱਲੋਂ ਇੱਥੇ ਲਿਆ ਕੇ ਸੰਸਕਾਰ ਕੀਤਾ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਸੀ।

ਇਹ ਗੁਰਦੁਆਰਾ ਸਾਨੂੰ ਸ਼ਹੀਦਾਂ ਦੀ ਕੁਰਬਾਨੀ ਅਤੇ ਅਟੱਲ ਵਿਸ਼ਵਾਸ ਦੀ ਯਾਦ ਦਿਵਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ। ਇੱਥੇ ਰੋਜ਼ਾਨਾ ਕੀਰਤਨ ਅਤੇ ਲੰਗਰ ਦੀ ਸੇਵਾ ਹੁੰਦੀ ਹੈ।
description_hi:
गुरुद्वारा शहीद गंज साहिब अमृतसर में स्थित एक पवित्र स्थल है, जो सिख शहीदों की स्मृति में बनाया गया है। 'शहीद गंज' का अर्थ है शहीदों का स्थान।

18वीं सदी के दौरान मुगल शासन में सिखों पर अत्याचार किए गए। कई सिखों को पकड़कर मार दिया गया, लेकिन उन्होंने अपने धर्म को नहीं छोड़ा।

शहीदों के सिर और शरीरों को यहाँ लाकर अंतिम संस्कार किया जाता था।

यह गुरुद्वारा शहीदों के बलिदान और अटूट विश्वास का प्रतीक है। यहाँ प्रतिदिन कीर्तन और लंगर की सेवा होती है।

description_en:
Gurdwara Sri Tarn Taran Sahib, located in the city of Tarn Taran in Punjab, is one of the most historically and spiritually significant Sikh shrines. It was founded by Guru Arjan Dev Ji, the fifth Sikh Guru, in the late 16th century and holds a special place in Sikh history due to its association with healing, humility, and spiritual upliftment.

The name 'Tarn Taran' translates to 'the boat that carries one across the worldly ocean,' symbolizing liberation from the cycle of birth and death through devotion and remembrance of Waheguru. This profound meaning reflects the spiritual essence of the Gurdwara and its purpose as a place of inner transformation.

Guru Arjan Dev Ji established this sacred site as a center for spiritual learning and service. He personally supervised the construction of the Sarovar (holy water tank), which is considered the largest among all Sikh Gurdwaras. The Sarovar is believed to possess healing properties, and for centuries, devotees have come here with deep faith to seek relief from physical and spiritual ailments.

Historically, the region of Tarn Taran was affected by diseases such as leprosy. Guru Arjan Dev Ji emphasized compassion and service toward those suffering from such illnesses. He encouraged people not to discriminate against the sick and to treat everyone with dignity and care. This message of inclusiveness and humanity became a defining characteristic of the Gurdwara.

The Sarovar at Tarn Taran Sahib is a central feature of the complex. Its vast expanse and calm waters create a serene and meditative atmosphere. Devotees often take a dip in the holy water as an act of faith, believing in its purifying and healing effects. The practice is accompanied by prayer and remembrance of the Divine.

The architecture of Gurdwara Sri Tarn Taran Sahib reflects traditional Sikh design, with a beautiful white marble structure, intricately decorated interiors, and a peaceful courtyard. The Darbar Sahib (main prayer hall) stands gracefully beside the Sarovar, providing a spiritually uplifting environment for visitors.

The Gurdwara complex also includes accommodations for pilgrims, a Langar hall, and various facilities that support the needs of visitors. The Langar at Tarn Taran Sahib continues the Sikh tradition of serving free meals to all, regardless of background, reinforcing the values of equality and community service.

A significant event associated with Tarn Taran Sahib is the annual 'Amavasya' (no-moon day) gathering, which attracts thousands of devotees from different parts of the country. On this day, the Gurdwara becomes a center of vibrant spiritual activity, with kirtan, katha, and collective prayers creating a powerful devotional atmosphere.

Throughout its history, Tarn Taran Sahib has remained a symbol of compassion, healing, and faith. It has played an important role in spreading Sikh teachings and promoting values such as humility, service, and devotion.

The Gurdwara also stands as a reminder of Guru Arjan Dev Ji’s vision of creating inclusive spaces where people from all walks of life could come together in prayer and service. His teachings continue to inspire visitors to lead lives rooted in spirituality and compassion.

Visiting Gurdwara Sri Tarn Taran Sahib is often described as a deeply calming and transformative experience. The peaceful surroundings, combined with the spiritual vibrations of Gurbani, help devotees find inner peace and clarity.

Today, the Gurdwara continues to serve as a beacon of hope and healing, attracting devotees not only from Punjab but from across the world. It remains a place where faith meets service, and where individuals are reminded of the power of devotion and the importance of living a life dedicated to the welfare of others.

ਗੁਰਦੁਆਰਾ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਤਰਨ ਤਾਰਨ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਪੰਜਾਬ ਦੇ ਤਰਨ ਤਾਰਨ ਸ਼ਹਿਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਸਥਿਤ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਇਸ ਦੀ ਸਥਾਪਨਾ ਪੰਜਵੇਂ ਸਿੱਖ ਗੁਰੂ, ਸ੍ਰੀ ਗੁਰੂ ਅਰਜਨ ਦੇਵ ਜੀ ਨੇ ਕੀਤੀ ਸੀ।

'ਤਰਨ ਤਾਰਨ' ਦਾ ਅਰਥ ਹੈ ਸੰਸਾਰਕ ਸਮੁੰਦਰ ਤੋਂ ਪਾਰ ਲੰਘਾਉਣ ਵਾਲਾ। ਇਹ ਗੁਰਦੁਆਰਾ ਆਤਮਿਕ ਉਤਥਾਨ ਅਤੇ ਮੁਕਤੀ ਦਾ ਪ੍ਰਤੀਕ ਹੈ।

ਇੱਥੇ ਦਾ ਸਰੋਵਰ ਸਿੱਖ ਧਰਮ ਦਾ ਸਭ ਤੋਂ ਵੱਡਾ ਸਰੋਵਰ ਮੰਨਿਆ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਇਸ ਨੂੰ ਚੰਗਾ ਕਰਨ ਵਾਲਾ ਮੰਨਿਆ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ।

ਗੁਰੂ ਅਰਜਨ ਦੇਵ ਜੀ ਨੇ ਇੱਥੇ ਬਿਮਾਰ ਲੋਕਾਂ ਦੀ ਸੇਵਾ ਅਤੇ ਸਹਾਇਤਾ 'ਤੇ ਜ਼ੋਰ ਦਿੱਤਾ।

ਅੱਜ ਇਹ ਗੁਰਦੁਆਰਾ ਸੇਵਾ, ਸਮਾਨਤਾ ਅਤੇ ਭਗਤੀ ਦਾ ਪ੍ਰਤੀਕ ਹੈ। ਇੱਥੇ ਰੋਜ਼ਾਨਾ ਲੰਗਰ ਅਤੇ ਕੀਰਤਨ ਹੁੰਦਾ ਹੈ।
description_hi:
गुरुद्वारा श्री तरन तारन साहिब पंजाब के तरन तारन शहर में स्थित है और इसकी स्थापना पांचवें सिख गुरु, गुरु अर्जन देव जी ने की थी।

'तरन तारन' का अर्थ है संसार के समुद्र से पार ले जाने वाला। यह गुरुद्वारा आध्यात्मिक मुक्ति और शांति का प्रतीक है।

यहाँ का सरोवर सिख धर्म का सबसे बड़ा सरोवर माना जाता है और इसे उपचारात्मक गुणों वाला माना जाता है।

गुरु अर्जन देव जी ने यहाँ बीमारों की सेवा और मानवता पर विशेष बल दिया।

आज यह गुरुद्वारा सेवा, समानता और भक्ति का प्रतीक है। यहाँ प्रतिदिन लंगर और कीर्तन होता है।

description_en:
Gurdwara Sri Hemkunt Sahib, nestled in the majestic Himalayan ranges of Uttarakhand at an altitude of approximately 4,329 meters (14,200 feet), is one of the most revered and spiritually uplifting Sikh pilgrimage sites. Surrounded by seven snow-capped peaks and situated beside a pristine glacial lake, this sacred place is deeply associated with Guru Gobind Singh Ji, the tenth Sikh Guru.

The name 'Hemkunt' translates to 'Lake of Snow,' perfectly describing the serene and breathtaking environment of the Gurdwara. According to Sikh tradition and references found in the autobiographical composition 'Bachittar Natak' within the Dasam Granth, Guru Gobind Singh Ji meditated at this very location in a previous life as a yogi devoted to the Divine.

The rediscovery of Hemkunt Sahib in the early 20th century is attributed to Sant Sohan Singh Ji and later Baba Modan Singh Ji, who undertook arduous efforts to identify and establish the site as described in Sikh scriptures. With immense dedication and community support, the Gurdwara was constructed in this remote and challenging terrain, making it accessible to devotees.

The journey to Hemkunt Sahib is considered a spiritual pilgrimage in itself. Pilgrims must undertake a कठिन trek of approximately 19 kilometers from Govindghat, passing through Ghangaria, which serves as the base camp. The steep and demanding path tests physical endurance and mental determination, symbolizing the effort required to attain spiritual elevation.

The Gurdwara remains open to devotees only for a limited period each year, typically from May to October, due to extreme weather conditions and heavy snowfall during the winter months. During the open season, thousands of pilgrims from across the world visit Hemkunt Sahib to seek spiritual solace and divine blessings.

The architecture of Gurdwara Sri Hemkunt Sahib is unique compared to other Sikh shrines. It features a star-shaped structure designed to withstand heavy snowfall and harsh weather conditions. The simplicity of the design blends harmoniously with the natural surroundings, enhancing the spiritual ambiance of the place.

Adjacent to the Gurdwara lies the sacred Hemkunt Lake, whose crystal-clear waters reflect the surrounding snow-covered peaks. Devotees often take a dip in the icy waters as an act of faith, despite the extremely low temperatures. This act is seen as a form of spiritual cleansing and devotion.

The Gurdwara complex provides basic facilities for pilgrims, including accommodation and Langar (community kitchen). Despite the challenging environment, volunteers tirelessly serve food and assist visitors, exemplifying the Sikh principle of 'Seva' (selfless service).

Daily prayers, kirtan, and recitation of Gurbani are conducted within the Gurdwara, creating a deeply spiritual and meditative atmosphere. The tranquility of the surroundings, combined with the sacred vibrations of Gurbani, offers a profound sense of peace and connection with the Divine.

Hemkunt Sahib is not just a physical destination but a spiritual journey that inspires self-discipline, humility, and devotion. The कठिन trek, the serene environment, and the divine association with Guru Gobind Singh Ji make this pilgrimage a transformative experience for many.

Visitors often describe their journey to Hemkunt Sahib as life-changing, as it allows them to disconnect from worldly distractions and immerse themselves in spiritual reflection. The site stands as a testament to the enduring strength of faith and the human spirit.

Today, Gurdwara Sri Hemkunt Sahib continues to inspire millions of devotees with its message of devotion, perseverance, and inner peace. It remains one of the highest and most spiritually significant Sikh shrines in the world, drawing pilgrims who seek both physical challenge and spiritual fulfillment.
description_pa:
ਗੁਰਦੁਆਰਾ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਹੇਮਕੁੰਟ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਉਤਰਾਖੰਡ ਦੇ ਚਮੋਲੀ ਜ਼ਿਲ੍ਹੇ ਵਿੱਚ ਹਿਮਾਲਿਆ ਦੀਆਂ ਪਹਾੜੀਆਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਸਥਿਤ ਹੈ। ਇਹ ਸਿੱਖ ਧਰਮ ਦਾ ਇੱਕ ਮਹੱਤਵਪੂਰਨ ਤੀਰਥ ਸਥਾਨ ਹੈ ਜੋ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਗੁਰੂ ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ਸਿੰਘ ਜੀ ਨਾਲ ਸੰਬੰਧਿਤ ਹੈ।

'ਹੇਮਕੁੰਟ' ਦਾ ਅਰਥ ਹੈ ਬਰਫ਼ ਦਾ ਝੀਲ। ਇਹ ਸਥਾਨ ਸੱਤ ਬਰਫ਼ੀਲੇ ਪਹਾੜਾਂ ਨਾਲ ਘਿਰਿਆ ਹੋਇਆ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਬਹੁਤ ਹੀ ਸ਼ਾਂਤ ਅਤੇ ਪਵਿੱਤਰ ਮਾਹੌਲ ਪ੍ਰਦਾਨ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ।

ਦਸਮ ਗ੍ਰੰਥ ਦੇ ਬਚਿੱਤਰ ਨਾਟਕ ਵਿੱਚ ਦਰਜ ਹੈ ਕਿ ਗੁਰੂ ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ਸਿੰਘ ਜੀ ਨੇ ਆਪਣੇ ਪਿਛਲੇ ਜਨਮ ਵਿੱਚ ਇੱਥੇ ਧਿਆਨ ਕੀਤਾ ਸੀ।

ਇੱਥੇ ਤੱਕ ਪਹੁੰਚਣ ਲਈ ਯਾਤਰੀਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਕਾਫ਼ੀ ਮੁਸ਼ਕਿਲ ਟ੍ਰੈਕ ਕਰਨਾ ਪੈਂਦਾ ਹੈ, ਜੋ ਆਤਮਿਕ ਯਾਤਰਾ ਦਾ ਪ੍ਰਤੀਕ ਹੈ।

ਇਹ ਗੁਰਦੁਆਰਾ ਸਾਲ ਵਿੱਚ ਕੁਝ ਮਹੀਨਿਆਂ ਲਈ ਹੀ ਖੁੱਲ੍ਹਦਾ ਹੈ। ਇੱਥੇ ਲੰਗਰ ਅਤੇ ਰਹਿਣ ਦੀ ਸਹੂਲਤ ਵੀ ਮਿਲਦੀ ਹੈ।
description_hi:
गुरुद्वारा श्री हेमकुंट साहिब उत्तराखंड के चमोली जिले में हिमालय की पहाड़ियों में स्थित है। यह सिख धर्म का एक अत्यंत पवित्र तीर्थ स्थल है, जो गुरु गोबिंद सिंह जी से संबंधित है।

'हेमकुंट' का अर्थ है बर्फ की झील। यह स्थान सात बर्फ से ढकी पहाड़ियों से घिरा हुआ है और अत्यंत शांत वातावरण प्रदान करता है।

दसम ग्रंथ के बचित्र नाटक में उल्लेख है कि गुरु गोबिंद सिंह जी ने अपने पूर्व जन्म में यहाँ तपस्या की थी।

यहाँ तक पहुँचने के लिए कठिन ट्रेक करना पड़ता है, जो आध्यात्मिक यात्रा का प्रतीक है।

यह गुरुद्वारा वर्ष में सीमित समय के लिए ही खुलता है और यहाँ लंगर व ठहरने की सुविधा उपलब्ध है।

description_en:
Gurdwara Rakab Ganj Sahib, located near the Parliament House in New Delhi, is one of the most historically significant Sikh shrines. This sacred site is associated with the martyrdom of Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji, the ninth Sikh Guru, and commemorates the place where his body was cremated after his execution in 1675.

Following the martyrdom of Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji at Chandni Chowk, his body was left unattended by the Mughal authorities as a warning to others. However, a devoted Sikh named Lakhi Shah Vanjara, along with his son Bhai Naghaiya Ji, undertook a courageous and risky mission to recover the Guru’s body under the cover of darkness.

Understanding the danger posed by the Mughal forces, Lakhi Shah Vanjara devised a unique plan to perform the last rites of the Guru Sahib. He placed the Guru’s body in a cart filled with hay and transported it to his residence, which was located at the site where Gurdwara Rakab Ganj Sahib stands today.

To avoid suspicion and interference from the Mughal authorities, Lakhi Shah Vanjara set his entire house on fire. This act of burning his own home served as a disguise for the cremation of Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji’s body. This extraordinary sacrifice demonstrated immense devotion, courage, and faith, and ensured that the Guru received proper last rites according to Sikh traditions.

The name 'Rakab Ganj' is believed to have originated from the presence of stables (rakab meaning stirrup) in the area during that time. Over the years, the site gained immense religious significance due to the historic event associated with it.

In 1783, Sardar Baghel Singh, a prominent Sikh leader, captured Delhi and took the initiative to build several historical Gurdwaras at important Sikh sites in the city. Gurdwara Rakab Ganj Sahib was constructed as part of this effort to preserve and honor Sikh heritage.

The Gurdwara has undergone several renovations and expansions over time, evolving into a magnificent structure with a large white marble complex, beautiful domes, and a peaceful environment that offers spiritual solace to visitors.

The architecture of the Gurdwara reflects traditional Sikh design, with a spacious prayer hall where devotees gather to listen to Gurbani and offer their prayers. The serene ambiance of the Gurdwara provides a stark contrast to the busy surroundings of the national capital.

Gurdwara Rakab Ganj Sahib is not only a place of worship but also a symbol of selfless sacrifice and unwavering devotion. It reminds visitors of the extraordinary lengths to which devotees went to honor their Guru, even at great personal risk.

The Gurdwara continues the Sikh tradition of Langar, serving free meals to all visitors regardless of caste, religion, or social status. This practice embodies the principles of equality and community service that are central to Sikhism.

Daily kirtan and recitation of Gurbani create a deeply spiritual atmosphere within the Gurdwara. Visitors often experience a sense of peace, humility, and reflection as they connect with the divine teachings of the Gurus.

The site holds immense historical importance as it represents not only the martyrdom of Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji but also the devotion of his followers. It serves as a reminder of the Sikh commitment to righteousness, justice, and the protection of human rights.

Today, Gurdwara Rakab Ganj Sahib stands as a beacon of faith and sacrifice in the heart of Delhi. It continues to inspire generations with its message of courage, devotion, and selfless service, encouraging individuals to uphold truth and stand against injustice in their lives.

ਗੁਰਦੁਆਰਾ ਰਕਾਬ ਗੰਜ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਨਵੀਂ ਦਿੱਲੀ ਵਿੱਚ ਸਥਿਤ ਇੱਕ ਮਹੱਤਵਪੂਰਨ ਸਿੱਖ ਇਤਿਹਾਸਕ ਸਥਾਨ ਹੈ। ਇਹ ਓਹ ਥਾਂ ਹੈ ਜਿੱਥੇ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਗੁਰੂ ਤੇਗ ਬਹਾਦਰ ਜੀ ਦੇ ਸ਼ਰੀਰ ਦਾ ਸੰਸਕਾਰ ਕੀਤਾ ਗਿਆ ਸੀ।

ਭਾਈ ਲੱਖੀ ਸ਼ਾਹ ਵਣਜਾਰਾ ਨੇ ਆਪਣੀ ਜਾਨ ਦੇ ਖ਼ਤਰੇ ਨੂੰ ਮੰਨਦੇ ਹੋਏ ਗੁਰੂ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਦੇ ਸ਼ਰੀਰ ਨੂੰ ਇੱਥੇ ਲਿਆ ਕੇ ਆਪਣੇ ਘਰ ਨੂੰ ਅੱਗ ਲਗਾ ਕੇ ਸੰਸਕਾਰ ਕੀਤਾ।

1783 ਵਿੱਚ ਸਰਦਾਰ ਬਘੇਲ ਸਿੰਘ ਨੇ ਇਸ ਗੁਰਦੁਆਰੇ ਦੀ ਸਥਾਪਨਾ ਕੀਤੀ।

ਇਹ ਸਥਾਨ ਸਿੱਖਾਂ ਦੀ ਭਗਤੀ, ਬਲਿਦਾਨ ਅਤੇ ਅਟੱਲ ਵਿਸ਼ਵਾਸ ਦਾ ਪ੍ਰਤੀਕ ਹੈ। ਇੱਥੇ ਰੋਜ਼ਾਨਾ ਲੰਗਰ ਅਤੇ ਕੀਰਤਨ ਹੁੰਦਾ ਹੈ।
description_hi:
गुरुद्वारा रकाब गंज साहिब नई दिल्ली में स्थित एक महत्वपूर्ण सिख ऐतिहासिक स्थल है। यह वही स्थान है जहाँ गुरु तेग बहादुर जी के शरीर का अंतिम संस्कार किया गया था।

भाई लखी शाह वंजारा ने अपने प्राणों की परवाह किए बिना गुरु जी के शरीर को यहाँ लाकर अपने घर को आग लगाकर उनका अंतिम संस्कार किया।

1783 में सरदार बघेल सिंह ने इस गुरुद्वारे का निर्माण कराया।

यह स्थल भक्ति, बलिदान और अटूट विश्वास का प्रतीक है। यहाँ प्रतिदिन लंगर और कीर्तन होता है।

description_en:
Gurdwara Sri Nanakmatta Sahib, located in the town of Nanakmatta in Uttarakhand, is a sacred Sikh shrine associated with Guru Nanak Dev Ji, the founder of Sikhism. This historic site holds immense spiritual significance as it marks the place where Guru Nanak Dev Ji visited during his first Udasi (spiritual journey) and spread the message of truth, humility, and devotion.

In ancient times, this place was known as 'Gorakhmata' and was a prominent center of yogis belonging to the Nath sect. These yogis practiced various forms of asceticism and believed in supernatural powers. When Guru Nanak Dev Ji arrived here, he engaged in deep spiritual discussions with the yogis, guiding them towards the path of true devotion and remembrance of the One Supreme Reality.

The yogis initially doubted Guru Nanak Dev Ji and attempted to challenge his spiritual authority. According to tradition, they used their mystical powers to test the Guru. One of the most well-known incidents associated with this place involves a sacred tree under which Guru Nanak Dev Ji was meditating. It is believed that the yogis caused the tree to dry up in an attempt to demonstrate their powers.

However, through his divine presence, Guru Nanak Dev Ji restored the tree to life. The tree, known as the 'Pipal tree' or 'Reetha Sahib tree,' is still preserved within the Gurdwara complex and is considered a living symbol of the Guru’s spiritual strength and divine grace.

Another remarkable aspect associated with this site is the 'Meetha Reetha' (sweet soapnut) tree. Normally, the fruit of the reetha tree is bitter, but it is believed that by Guru Nanak Dev Ji’s blessing, the fruits of this particular tree became sweet. This miracle symbolized the transformation of bitterness into sweetness through the Guru’s teachings.

Through his teachings and divine wisdom, Guru Nanak Dev Ji emphasized that true spirituality lies not in outward rituals or supernatural displays, but in living a life of honesty, humility, and constant remembrance of Waheguru. His interaction with the yogis led many of them to renounce their ego and accept the path of devotion.

After Guru Nanak Dev Ji’s visit, the place came to be known as 'Nanakmatta,' meaning 'the place sanctified by Guru Nanak’s wisdom.' Over time, it became an important center of Sikh pilgrimage.

The present Gurdwara was established and developed over the years to honor the Guru’s visit and preserve the historical significance of the site. The complex features a beautiful white structure, a serene Sarovar (holy water tank), and well-maintained surroundings that provide a peaceful spiritual environment for devotees.

The Sarovar at Nanakmatta Sahib is a focal point of the Gurdwara. Devotees often take a dip in its waters as an act of faith and spiritual cleansing. The calm and tranquil atmosphere of the Sarovar enhances the meditative experience.

The Gurdwara complex also includes facilities such as Langar, accommodation for pilgrims, and spaces for religious gatherings. The Langar continues the Sikh tradition of serving free meals to all visitors, promoting equality and selfless service.

Daily recitation of Gurbani and kirtan create a deeply spiritual ambiance within the Gurdwara. Visitors often experience a sense of inner peace and connection with the divine while spending time at the shrine.

Gurdwara Sri Nanakmatta Sahib is not only a place of worship but also a center of spiritual learning. It teaches the importance of humility, the rejection of ego, and the value of living a truthful and compassionate life.

Today, the Gurdwara attracts thousands of devotees from across India and beyond. It stands as a testament to Guru Nanak Dev Ji’s universal message of love, unity, and devotion to one God.

The legacy of Guru Nanak Dev Ji at Nanakmatta Sahib continues to inspire people to rise above divisions and embrace a life of simplicity, service, and spiritual awareness. The site remains a beacon of faith and a reminder of the transformative power of divine wisdom.

ਪੁਰਾਤਨ ਸਮੇਂ ਇਹ ਥਾਂ ਗੋਰਖਮੱਤਾ ਦੇ ਨਾਮ ਨਾਲ ਜਾਣੀ ਜਾਂਦੀ ਸੀ ਅਤੇ ਇੱਥੇ ਜੋਗੀ ਵੱਸਦੇ ਸਨ। ਗੁਰੂ ਨਾਨਕ ਦੇਵ ਜੀ ਨੇ ਇੱਥੇ ਆ ਕੇ ਜੋਗੀਆਂ ਨਾਲ ਵਿਚਾਰ-ਵਟਾਂਦਰਾ ਕੀਤਾ ਅਤੇ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਸੱਚੀ ਭਗਤੀ ਦਾ ਮਾਰਗ ਦਿਖਾਇਆ।

ਇੱਥੇ ਰੀਠੇ ਦਾ ਦਰੱਖਤ ਮਸ਼ਹੂਰ ਹੈ ਜਿਸ ਦੇ ਫਲ ਗੁਰੂ ਜੀ ਦੀ ਕਿਰਪਾ ਨਾਲ ਮਿੱਠੇ ਹੋ ਗਏ।

ਇਸ ਸਥਾਨ ਦਾ ਨਾਮ ਬਾਅਦ ਵਿੱਚ ਨਾਨਕਮੱਤਾ ਰੱਖਿਆ ਗਿਆ।

ਅੱਜ ਇਹ ਗੁਰਦੁਆਰਾ ਸ਼ਾਂਤੀ, ਸੇਵਾ ਅਤੇ ਭਗਤੀ ਦਾ ਪ੍ਰਤੀਕ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਇੱਥੇ ਲੰਗਰ ਅਤੇ ਸਰੋਵਰ ਦੀ ਸਹੂਲਤ ਹੈ।

प्राचीन समय में यह स्थान गोरखमता के नाम से जाना जाता था और यहाँ योगी निवास करते थे। गुरु नानक देव जी ने यहाँ आकर उन्हें सच्ची भक्ति का मार्ग दिखाया।

यहाँ रीठा का पेड़ प्रसिद्ध है, जिसके फल गुरु जी की कृपा से मीठे हो गए।

बाद में इस स्थान का नाम नानकमत्ता रखा गया।

आज यह गुरुद्वारा शांति, सेवा और भक्ति का प्रतीक है, जहाँ लंगर और सरोवर की सुविधा उपलब्ध है।

description_en:
Gurdwara Janam Asthan Nankana Sahib, located in the city of Nankana Sahib in present-day Pakistan, is one of the most sacred and historically significant sites in Sikhism. This holy shrine marks the birthplace of Guru Nanak Dev Ji, the founder of Sikhism, who was born here in 1469. The site holds immense spiritual importance as it represents the beginning of a divine mission that transformed the spiritual landscape of the world.

Originally known as 'Rai Bhoi Di Talwandi,' the town was later renamed Nankana Sahib in honor of Guru Nanak Dev Ji. From his early childhood, Guru Nanak Dev Ji displayed extraordinary spiritual insight, compassion, and a deep connection with the Divine. His teachings emphasized the oneness of God, equality of all human beings, and the importance of living a truthful and honest life.

The Janam Asthan (birthplace) is the very location where Guru Nanak Dev Ji spent his early years. It was here that he began questioning societal norms, ritualistic practices, and divisions based on caste and religion. His spiritual inclination and divine wisdom became evident at a very young age, attracting people from different backgrounds.

One of the most famous incidents associated with his childhood at this place is the 'True Bargain' (Sacha Sauda), where Guru Nanak Dev Ji used the money given by his father to feed hungry saints and the poor, demonstrating that true profit lies in serving humanity. Though this event took place nearby, it reflects the values he embodied from his early years at Nankana Sahib.

Another significant aspect of his early life was his refusal to accept the sacred thread (Janeu) ceremony, which symbolized caste distinctions. Guru Nanak Dev Ji explained that true purity comes from inner righteousness and devotion, not from external symbols. This message laid the foundation for the egalitarian principles of Sikhism.

The present structure of Gurdwara Janam Asthan Nankana Sahib was built and expanded over time, particularly during the Sikh Empire under Maharaja Ranjit Singh. The Gurdwara features a grand white marble complex with beautiful domes, intricate artwork, and a serene environment that reflects its spiritual significance.

The shrine includes the sanctified area believed to be the exact birthplace of Guru Nanak Dev Ji. Devotees from across the world visit this sacred site to pay their respects and connect with the origins of Sikhism.

Nankana Sahib has also been a site of significant historical events in more recent times. In 1921, a tragic incident known as the Nankana Sahib massacre took place, where peaceful Sikh reformers were attacked while seeking to free the Gurdwara from corrupt management. This event played a crucial role in the Gurdwara Reform Movement, leading to the establishment of proper Sikh management of Gurdwaras.

The Gurdwara complex offers facilities for pilgrims, including accommodation and Langar, where free meals are served to all visitors. The tradition of Langar continues to reflect the Sikh values of equality, service, and community.

Daily recitation of Gurbani and kirtan fills the Gurdwara with a deeply spiritual atmosphere. Visitors often experience a profound sense of peace and connection with the teachings of Guru Nanak Dev Ji.

Gurdwara Janam Asthan Nankana Sahib is not just a place of worship but a symbol of the birth of a universal message that transcends boundaries. It represents the beginning of a spiritual journey that emphasized love, equality, and devotion to one God.

For Sikhs and spiritual seekers worldwide, visiting this sacred site is considered a deeply emotional and transformative experience. It allows them to connect with the roots of Sikhism and reflect on the timeless teachings of Guru Nanak Dev Ji.

Today, Nankana Sahib continues to stand as a beacon of faith, unity, and spiritual awakening. It inspires millions to follow the path of truth, compassion, and selfless service, as taught by Guru Nanak Dev Ji.

description_en:
Gurdwara Panja Sahib, located in Hasan Abdal in the Punjab province of Pakistan, is one of the most sacred and historically significant Sikh shrines. It is closely associated with Guru Nanak Dev Ji, the founder of Sikhism, and is renowned for the miraculous imprint of the Guru’s hand (Panja) preserved on a large rock within the Gurdwara complex.

The history of Panja Sahib dates back to the early 16th century during Guru Nanak Dev Ji’s travels (Udasis). At that time, Hasan Abdal was a dry and arid region suffering from a severe shortage of water. A local Muslim saint named Wali Qandhari lived on a nearby hill and controlled the only source of water in the area.

When Guru Nanak Dev Ji arrived in Hasan Abdal along with his companion Bhai Mardana Ji, they found the local population struggling due to the scarcity of water. Bhai Mardana Ji, feeling thirsty, approached Wali Qandhari and requested water. However, Wali Qandhari, filled with pride and arrogance, refused to share water and challenged Guru Nanak Dev Ji’s spiritual authority.

Upon hearing this, Guru Nanak Dev Ji calmly instructed Bhai Mardana Ji to return without argument. The Guru then sat in meditation and, by divine grace, caused a fresh spring of water to emerge from the ground at the base of the hill. This new source of water began to flow freely, providing relief to the people of the area.

Witnessing this miracle, Wali Qandhari became furious as his own water source began to dry up. In anger, he pushed a massive boulder down the hill towards Guru Nanak Dev Ji, intending to harm him. As the rock rolled down with great force, Guru Nanak Dev Ji raised his hand and stopped it effortlessly.

The rock halted instantly upon touching the Guru’s hand, leaving a clear imprint of his palm on its surface. This miraculous event demonstrated the power of divine grace over ego and arrogance. The handprint, known as the 'Panja,' is still visible today and is the central feature of the Gurdwara.

This घटना carries a profound spiritual message. It emphasizes humility, compassion, and the importance of sharing resources with others. Guru Nanak Dev Ji’s actions showed that true spiritual power lies in serving humanity and trusting in the Divine.

The site where this miracle occurred was later developed into Gurdwara Panja Sahib. The Gurdwara complex includes the sacred rock with the handprint, a Sarovar (holy water tank) formed by the flowing spring, and a beautifully constructed shrine that attracts pilgrims from around the world.

The architecture of the Gurdwara reflects traditional Sikh design, with a white marble structure, elegant domes, and a peaceful environment that enhances the spiritual experience of visitors.

One of the most significant events associated with Panja Sahib in modern history occurred during the time of the partition of India in 1947. Sikh refugees traveling by train were attacked, and when a train carrying Sikh pilgrims was stopped near Hasan Abdal, local Sikhs risked their lives to provide food and water to the passengers. This act of seva and sacrifice is remembered with deep respect.

Today, Gurdwara Panja Sahib is an important pilgrimage site, especially during the festival of Vaisakhi, when thousands of devotees gather to pay their respects and participate in religious ceremonies.

The Gurdwara continues to uphold the Sikh tradition of Langar, serving free meals to all visitors regardless of their background. This practice reinforces the message of equality and selfless service.

Visitors often feel a deep sense of peace and spiritual connection when they witness the sacred handprint and reflect on the teachings of Guru Nanak Dev Ji. The site serves as a reminder of the triumph of humility over ego and the power of faith.

Gurdwara Panja Sahib stands today as a symbol of divine grace, compassion, and unity. It continues to inspire millions to live a life of service, humility, and devotion to the welfare of all humanity.

description_en:
Gurdwara Darbar Sahib Kartarpur, located in Kartarpur in the Narowal district of Punjab, Pakistan, is one of the most sacred and historically significant sites in Sikhism. This revered shrine marks the place where Guru Nanak Dev Ji, the founder of Sikhism, spent the final years of his life and eventually merged with the Divine in 1539.

After completing his extensive spiritual journeys (Udasis) across different parts of the world, Guru Nanak Dev Ji settled in Kartarpur around 1522. Here, he established a spiritual community based on the principles of equality, honest living, and devotion to one God. Kartarpur became the first organized Sikh community, setting the foundation for the Sikh way of life.

At Kartarpur, Guru Nanak Dev Ji introduced and practiced the concept of 'Kirat Karo, Naam Japo, Vand Chhako'—earn honestly, remember the Divine, and share with others. These teachings became central to Sikh philosophy and continue to guide millions of followers worldwide.

One of the most significant contributions of Guru Nanak Dev Ji at Kartarpur was the establishment of the institution of Langar (community kitchen). People from all backgrounds, regardless of caste, religion, or social status, sat together and shared meals, symbolizing equality and unity.

Guru Nanak Dev Ji also led a simple life as a farmer during his time in Kartarpur. He emphasized the dignity of labor and demonstrated that spirituality and worldly responsibilities can coexist harmoniously. His daily routine included meditation, singing of Gurbani (kirtan), and working in the fields.

Kartarpur became a center of spiritual learning, attracting followers from far and wide. Devotees gathered here to listen to the Guru’s teachings and experience a life based on truth and humility.

One of the most profound events associated with Kartarpur Sahib is Guru Nanak Dev Ji’s departure from the physical world. According to tradition, both Hindus and Muslims claimed the Guru as their own and wished to perform his last rites according to their respective customs. However, when the cloth covering his body was lifted, only flowers were found, symbolizing the unity of humanity and the transcendence of religious divisions. The flowers were then divided, with each community performing their rites.

The Gurdwara Darbar Sahib Kartarpur stands at the site associated with this event, making it a deeply emotional and spiritually significant place for devotees.

The present structure of the Gurdwara has been renovated and expanded over time, especially in recent years, making it accessible to pilgrims through the Kartarpur Corridor. This corridor allows devotees from India to visit the shrine without a visa, strengthening spiritual and cultural connections.

The architecture of the Gurdwara is grand and serene, featuring white marble, expansive courtyards, and a peaceful environment that reflects the simplicity and purity of Guru Nanak Dev Ji’s teachings.

The Gurdwara complex provides facilities for pilgrims, including Langar and resting areas. The tradition of Langar continues to embody the principles of equality, service, and community.

Daily prayers, kirtan, and recitation of Gurbani create a deeply spiritual atmosphere. Visitors often describe a profound sense of peace and connection when they visit Kartarpur Sahib, as it represents the culmination of Guru Nanak Dev Ji’s earthly journey.

Gurdwara Darbar Sahib Kartarpur is not only a place of worship but also a symbol of unity, equality, and spiritual enlightenment. It represents the essence of Guru Nanak Dev Ji’s teachings and the beginning of a collective Sikh identity.

Today, Kartarpur Sahib continues to inspire millions across the world. It stands as a beacon of peace, reminding humanity of the importance of living a life rooted in truth, compassion, and selfless service. The legacy of Guru Nanak Dev Ji at this sacred place continues to guide generations toward spiritual awakening and universal brotherhood.
